reconstructed_captions.28: A hand applies contact cement to the edges of the leather pieces.
reconstructed_captions.29: The leather and fabric liner are carefully aligned and pressed together.
reconstructed_captions.30: A wing divider scores a stitching guideline parallel to the leather's edge.
reconstructed_captions.31: A multi-pronged stitching iron is positioned on the guideline.
reconstructed_captions.32: A mallet strikes the iron, punching a row of stitching holes through the layers.
reconstructed_captions.33: The hole punching continues around the entire piece.
reconstructed_captions.34: The leather piece is clamped into a stitching pony to hold it steady.
reconstructed_captions.35: A length of waxed thread is prepared with a needle on each end.
reconstructed_captions.36: The hand-stitching begins, using a two-needle saddle stitch technique.
reconstructed_captions.37: The stitching continues steadily along the pre-punched holes.
reconstructed_captions.38: A close-up shows the thread being pulled tight after each stitch.
reconstructed_captions.39: The final stitches are made and secured with a backstitch.
reconstructed_captions.40: The excess thread is neatly trimmed with a pair of snips.
reconstructed_captions.41: The location for a snap fastener is marked on the leather flap.
reconstructed_captions.42: A circular punch and mallet are used to create a hole for the snap.
reconstructed_captions.43: The components of a metal snap are inserted into the hole.
reconstructed_captions.44: A setter tool is placed over the snap hardware on top of an anvil.
reconstructed_captions.45: A hammer strikes the tool once to begin setting the snap in place.
